comparator.name: Biomedical Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: UvA builds from cells, genetics, anatomy and physiology to laboratory work, immunology, cell imaging and genome analysis. This plan illustrates Frontiers in Medical Biology. Students then take electives and complete an independent biomedical research placement.
components: Basiswiskunde en Statistiek in de Biomedische wetenschappen
Voortgezette Statistiek in de Biomedische wetenschappen
Regulering van vorm en functie van dieren
Mechanismen van ziekten van de mens
Data Science in de Biomedische wetenschappen
Choose one course from the specialisation’s approved options.
Choose from the programme’s elective options.
Carry out independent biomedical research during a placement and write a report in English.

core: Human biology from molecules and cells to tissues, organs and the whole body
Molecular cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, omics and systems biology
Mechanisms, causes, diagnosis, prevention and treatment of human disease
Experimental, laboratory, imaging and independent biomedical research
Biomedical statistics, data science and genome-scale analysis
adjacent: Personalised medicine and translation from biomedical discovery to healthcare
Bioethics, prevention, public health and biomedical communication
questions: How do healthy and diseased human bodies function from molecules to organs?
How can genetic, omics, imaging and experimental methods explain disease mechanisms?
How can biomedical evidence support prevention, diagnosis and more personalised treatment?

alternatives.label: Human biology and disease research
alternatives.concept: Study what happens when cells, tissues and organs stop working normally. Build from genetics, anatomy and physiology to laboratory methods, infection, disease mechanisms and pharmacology.
alternatives.labelReason: The official degree centres on the human body, disease mechanisms, molecular and cellular biology, microbiology, immunology, laboratory work and independent biomedical research.
progression: The life sciences foundation precedes cellular biology, anatomy, physiology and laboratory work. Evolutionary genetics and molecular biology support later pathology. Mathematics and experimental methods precede advanced statistics and research synthesis.

alternatives.label: Population health and disease prevention
alternatives.concept: Study why disease affects some populations more than others. Connect epidemiology and human biology with health behaviour, social conditions and public policy to examine prevention and intervention.
alternatives.labelReason: Prevention, translation to healthcare and Patient Oriented Research provide a direct basis for a population-level health and intervention programme.
alternatives.distinctness: Differs from Human biology and disease research by 60 EC each way. It emphasises prevention, health behaviour, social inquiry and policy.
progression: Epidemiology and introductory sociology lead into qualitative research, health psychology and communication. Statistics precedes public economics. Cell biology and physiology prepare for advanced study of infection and disease.

alternatives.label: Quantitative methods for biomedical questions
alternatives.concept: Use programming, mathematics and statistics to study biomedical questions. Develop methods for analysing images and signals, modelling systems and building predictions alongside courses in physiology, molecular genetics and disease.
alternatives.labelReason: The programme's distinctive omics and systems-biology line, genome analysis, biomedical statistics, data science and personalised-treatment questions support a quantitative biomedical route.
alternatives.distinctness: Differs from Human biology and disease research by 45 EC and from Population health and disease prevention by 90 EC each way. It emphasises image and signal analysis, prediction and numerical modelling.
progression: Python precedes image processing and data preparation. Mathematics precedes linear algebra, signal analysis, numerical methods and deep learning. Lab work and molecular-cell biology support later genetics and disease study.

candidates.label: Neurobiology and neurological disease
candidates.reason: Comparative neurobiology, perception and higher brain functions offer a credible direction. They already strengthen the closest option, while a separate route would cover less of the degree’s broader experimental and quantitative identity than the retained options.

routeSelection.basis: Frontiers in Medical Biology extends the common molecular, genomic and experimental research sequence across biomedical systems. Neurobiology centres on the nervous system and Patient Oriented Research on research closer to clinical applications. This choice follows the breadth of the UvA core independently of UCR fit. The standard 18 EC project leaves 12 EC open.

selection.assessment: Three UCR options provide distinct study in disease mechanisms, prevention and quantitative methods. The quantitative option develops transferable methods for biomedical questions. The dedicated omics and research placement remain specific to the UvA curriculum.

Both study how disease affects human organ systems.
Both study biomolecules, enzymes and metabolism.
Both examine cell structure and function and the molecular processes that regulate them.
Both study immune mechanisms. UvA includes a dedicated immunology practical.
Both develop practical molecular techniques. UCR includes DNA isolation, PCR and electrophoresis.

notes.text: UvA combines an integrated laboratory sequence, dedicated omics study and a required research placement. The UCR options combine individual courses in biomedical science, population health or quantitative methods. Their laboratory and research experiences differ from UvA’s required sequence.

audience.programmeDescription: UvA Biomedical Sciences studies how the human body works and how disease develops. The programme combines laboratory work, data analysis and independent biomedical research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options explore disease mechanisms, population health or quantitative methods. UvA brings these areas together in a specialist biomedical curriculum.
